clauses.reason: The sole paragraph provides that Executive Order No. 9512 of January 16, 1945 “is hereby revoked”. The order states no effective date, so the revocation took effect when signed on December 20, 1949. The filing stamp on the page reads December 22, 1949; that later filing date is disclosed as the alternative date if effectiveness is tied to filing, and the order itself does not say so. The command was exhausted by performance and the end source is the order's own text.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10093 (14 FR 7681 (Federal Register of December 23, 1949)) was signed December 20, 1949. The filing stamp printed after the order reads December 22, 1949, two days after signing. Its held Federal Register text, registered as the original representation for this order, prints the order number, its title and the signing date, and its operative command is the sentence providing that Executive Order No. 9512 of January 16, 1945 “is hereby revoked”. On 2026-10-14 the command is terminated: a revoking command is complete when it takes effect, and this order states no separate effective date, so it took effect when signed on December 20, 1949. The order contains no condition, postponement, report, transfer or continuing duty. The only other held text containing this order's number is the Federal Register page that reproduces this same order (EO_10092.txt, issue of December 23, 1949); it is the same instrument, not a later one. The Federal Register disposition-note search, the U.S. Code citation search and the eCFR citation search each report no hit naming this order; the last two test only for current citations and are cited as bounded searches. The surviving consequence is that Executive Order No. 9512 of January 16, 1945, which provided for coordination of the allocations of field positions subject to the Classification Act of 1923, as amended remains revoked; that consequence follows from the performed command and is not a command that still has to end.
